key_insight: GeONet improves flow-field prediction in porous media by explicitly encoding geometry alongside material properties and coordinates, enabling stronger cross-geometry generalization than a DeepONet baseline.
engineering_relevance: The model can accelerate pressure-field prediction for microfluidic experiments, tracer-test interpretation, and digital-twin workflows where many heterogeneous pore geometries must be evaluated quickly.
method: Extends the Branch-Trunk operator network with a Leaf Network that encodes the binary solid-void mask.
Uses porosity, permeability, coordinates, and local geometric descriptors with random Fourier features.
Fuses representations with a gated DeepMixer to predict steady-state pressure.
evidence_signal: Trained on 5,000 PFLOTRAN simulations (~30 TB) and evaluated on held-out and unseen geometries, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0381–0.0676 and R2 of 0.9511–0.9822, substantially outperforming DeepONet.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality geometry masks and large simulation datasets, so deployment may be limited when geometry encoding is noisy or training coverage is sparse.
paper_title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network for Predicting Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
